correctness_confidence.basis: The analytic reduction, Horn lower certificates, chamber-vertex upper-bound logic, padding argument, and exact rational witnesses are coherent. All 875 supplied tiling certificates passed fresh exact verification; exact upper-chain replay was sampled completely through m=5 rather than rerun for every m<=9.

rigor.basis: The finite theorem is reduced to explicit exact proof objects: LR-positive Horn triples for lower bounds and exact rational chamber vertices plus dimension-at-most-three Horn feasibility for upper bounds. Convexity correctly extends vertex feasibility to each full chamber. Conjectural and numerical extensions are clearly separated.

novelty.basis: The inertia-(m,3) chamber formulas, tiling certificates, block-shift upper constructions, and padding phase appear distinct from the checked commutator-norm literature. Priority remains bounded by the literature search and the inaccessible earlier AIRR line.

significance.basis: The work gives a substantial finite classification through d=14, proves an all-m family of lower bounds, and identifies a genuine zero-padding phase and rank jump. It also supplies a concrete route toward a general formula.

reproducibility.basis: The exact certificate corpus is portable and verifies without pickles. Fresh replays confirmed all lower certificates, exposedness witnesses, family-A instances, padding margins, and exact upper chains for m<=5. Full exact upper replay at m=6,...,9 is substantially slower and was not repeated in this assessment.

summary: A strong computer-assisted classification of the inverse self-commutator cost on inertia-(m,3) strata for m=3,...,9 and z<=2. The lower and upper halves are logically complementary and exact: Horn tilings prove each candidate form, while block-shift chain feasibility at exact chamber vertices plus convexity proves the matching upper bound. The all-m family-A theorem and the finite padding/rank statements are well supported. No material objection was found.
strengths: The Horn-program formulation turns the nonlinear self-commutator problem into a finite spectral optimisation with a clear objective.
Every finite lower bound is represented by a compact integer tiling certificate whose LR condition and coefficient identity can be checked independently.
The upper construction uses only Hermitian-sum feasibility in dimensions at most three, and the projection/convexity argument from chamber vertices is sound.
Theorem 2 extracts a dimension-free analytic family from the finite computation.
The padding failure is demonstrated by exact rational margins, and the m=4 rank jump is formulated as an exact optimal-face statement.
Numerical extensions and the six-family generalisation are explicitly labelled as evidence and conjecture.
weaknesses: The principal classification is a large computer-assisted finite result; human verification of all upper witnesses without running the supplied exact code is impractical.
The six-family description lacks a general proof for families B-F and for upper feasibility, so the conceptual general-m theorem remains open.
Several background reductions and boundary comparisons are inherited from earlier AIRR records that were outside the permitted source set.
strong_novelty_candidates: Exact inertia-(m,3) chamber classifications for m=3,...,9 and z<=2.
Horn tiling certificates paired with 3x3 block-shift chains as matching lower and upper proof objects.
The modulo-three padding phase and exact m=4 increase in minimum optimal rank after zero padding.
